ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a protractor is combined with a triangular plate with an angle of $30^\circ$ ($\angle CAB=30^\circ$). The hypotenuse AB of the triangular plate coincides with the diameter MN of the circle on which the protractor lies. Now, point P is exactly the midpoint of the semicircular arc of the protractor, and we connect CP. If BC = 4, what is the length of CP?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let the intersection of CP and AB be H, construct $HI\perp BC$ at I, and $HJ\perp AP$ at J,\\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of the semicircle, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ C lies on the semicircle Q where the protractor is located, and P is the midpoint of $\overset{\frown}{APB}$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCP=\angle ACP=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $CI=HI$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CAB=30^\circ$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle IBH=60^\circ$, $\angle IHB=30^\circ$,\\
Let $BI=x$, then $BH=2x$, $HI=\sqrt{3}x$, $CI=4−x$,\\
$\therefore$ $4−x=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
Solving yields: $x=2\sqrt{3}−2$,\\
$\therefore$ $BH=2(2\sqrt{3}-2)=4\sqrt{3}-4$, $CH=\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{3}(2\sqrt{3}-2)=6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6}$,\\
Similarly, it can be obtained that: $AB=2BC=8$,\\
$\therefore$ $AH=8−BH=12-4\sqrt{3}$,\\
Similarly, it can be obtained that: $\angle JAH=45^\circ$, $HJ=AJ=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AH=6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6}$,\\
And $\angle HPJ=\angle ABC=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $HP=\frac{HJ}{\sin 60^\circ}=4\sqrt{6}-4\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CP=4\sqrt{6}-4\sqrt{2}+6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6}=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{6}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, a protractor is combined with a triangular plate with an angle of $30^\circ$ ($\angle CAB=30^\circ$). The hypotenuse $AB$ of the triangular plate coincides with the diameter $MN$ of the circle on which the protractor lies. Point $P$ is the midpoint of the semicircular arc, and $CP$ is connected. If $BC=4$, what is the length of $CP$?
raw_record.answer:
Let the intersection of $CP$ and $AB$ be $H$, construct $HI\perp BC$ at $I$, and $HJ\perp AP$ at $J$.\\
Because $AB$ is the diameter of the semicircle, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.\\
Therefore $C$ lies on the semicircle, and $P$ is the midpoint of arc $\overset{\frown}{APB}$.\\
So $\angle BCP=\angle ACP=45^\circ$.\\
Thus $CI=HI$.\\
Because $\angle CAB=30^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\angle IBH=60^\circ$, $\angle IHB=30^\circ$.\\
Let $BI=x$, then $BH=2x$, $HI=\sqrt{3}x$, $CI=4-x$.\\
So $4-x=\sqrt{3}x$.\\
Solving gives $x=2\sqrt{3}-2$.\\
Hence $BH=2(2\sqrt{3}-2)=4\sqrt{3}-4$, and $CH=\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{3}(2\sqrt{3}-2)=6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6}$.\\
Also $AB=2BC=8$.\\
So $AH=8-BH=12-4\sqrt{3}$.\\
Also $\angle JAH=45^\circ$, and $HJ=AJ=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AH=6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6}$.\\
And $\angle HPJ=\angle ABC=60^\circ$.\\
Therefore $HP=\frac{HJ}{\sin 60^\circ}=4\sqrt{6}-4\sqrt{2}$.\\
Thus $CP=HP+CH=(4\sqrt{6}-4\sqrt{2})+(6\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{6})=2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{6}$.

Point P is located on the semicircular arc above and slightly to the right of the protractor, and CP is connected in the figure.

Reasoning: Using the coordinate method, take C=(0,0), and let BC be vertically upward. It is known that BC=4, so B=(0,4). Also because ∠CAB=30°, and the set square in the figure has a right angle at C, triangle ABC is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, and BC is the side opposite 30°, so AC=4√3, A=(4√3,0).

AB is the diameter of the semicircle, so the center O is the midpoint of AB: O=((0+4√3)/2,(4+0)/2)=(2√3,2). The radius is AB/2=4.
